verdict: Meta's ad business grew revenue 28% to $60.8B — but costs rose even faster (R&D up 67%, a $2.4B legal charge, $1.2B of severance), so operating profit fell 8% and free cash flow shrank to just $784M.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: operating cash flow was $31.9B — capex took nearly all of it

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp — 98% of Meta's money. Ad impressions rose 14% and the average price per ad rose 12%.

segments.name: Family of Apps other revenue
segments.note: Non-ad income from the apps — WhatsApp business messaging, subscriptions and other fees; up 73% YoY.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.note: Quest headsets and AI glasses; revenue up 16%, but the segment lost $4.6B this quarter building them.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI research and product engineering — up 67% YoY as Meta races to build superintelligence; now 36% of all revenue.

opex.name: Marketing & sales
opex.note: Selling ads and promoting Meta's apps and devices.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: The back office, including $2.4B of legal charges recognized this quarter.

otherDetail: Interest and other income (expense), net was a $19M expense — interest earned on Meta's cash roughly offset by interest and other costs.

takeaways.title: The ad machine is still growing fast
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 28% to $60.8B — impressions up 14%, price per ad up 12%, and 3.60 billion people use a Meta app daily.

takeaways.title: But profit fell anyway
takeaways.text: Total costs jumped 55%: R&D up 67% to $21.7B, plus $2.4B of legal charges and $1.18B of severance from the May layoffs (about 8,000 roles). Operating income fell 8% to $18.8B, and Reality Labs lost another $4.6B.

takeaways.title: Free cash flow nearly vanished
takeaways.text: Operations generated $31.9B of cash, but data-center and AI spending consumed almost all of it — free cash flow was just $784M. Meta now guides 2026 capex (incl. finance leases) to $130–145B.

oneTimers: $2.40B of charges related to legal proceedings are inside this quarter's costs (in general & administrative), and $1.18B of severance from the May 2026 headcount reduction is spread across the cost lines. Meta raised its full-year expense outlook to $165–169B to absorb the legal charges.
